Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot credits: emergency request to finish evaluation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the warm intro last week. We're in the middle of a two-week pilot and unexpectedly exhausted the credits allocated to our account this morning. We have two engineering teams who spun up parallel experiments under related sub-orgs — I realize that was a coordination fail on our side.

Can Redwood authorize a short-term extension (another 50k token equivalent) so we can finish the last set of quality checks? We are close to a purchase decision but need the final eval to complete the scorecards. We've asked procurement to loop in a PO if needed — copied here.

I attached the console screenshot and can send export if helpful. Appreciate a rapid take — we can also do a quick call.

Best,
Maria
Maria Gutierrez
Director of ML Platforms, Upscale AI

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the note and the screenshot. I'm glad the pilot is progressing. Before I escalate to get an emergency top-up approved, can you confirm two quick things so we have an audit trail:

- Which sub-orgs/teams within Upscale ran the parallel experiments (names or team ids)
- Approx token consumption per run and whether these were concurrently launched from the same project

If you can attach the usage export (CSV) that will speed things up. Our policy allows one discretionary extension for active pilots, but we do have guardrails when multiple parallel accounts are involved — want to make sure we're not open to accidental duplication or a recurring pattern.

I'll copy our renewals lead Ben and loop in ops if we need a short-term emergency grant. If desirable, happy to get legal/procurement on a call to accelerate.

Karthik

karthik@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pilot credits: emergency request to finish evaluation

Team — forwarding Upscale's request. They hit their pilot allocation after running two concurrent team experiments. Attached CSV shows two distinct project ids that map back to the same billing org.

Quick ask: can we approve a one-time, conditioned extension here? Flags: multiple parallel runs, recent extension granted in Dec 2026 (see account history), and procurement is already in the loop which suggests they may convert fast.

Proposals I'm considering:
- Temporary 50k token grant scoped to the existing projects, expire in 7 days
- Require SSO provisioning or proof of org ownership before activating
- Legal to prepare a short addendum that converts the extension into a paid pilot credit if they convert within 30 days

Priyom — can you run a lightweight abuse check (IPs, billing addresses, prior trial patterns)? Laura — if we approve, I'll coordinate with CS for onboarding and legal for the addendum.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot credits: emergency request to finish evaluation

Karthik / Laura —

I've completed a preliminary check. Summary below (full notes attached):

Findings:
- The two project ids in the CSV resolve to accounts that share the same billing email and company domain (upscale.ai) — consistent with Maria's explanation.
- There are three previous extension events for Upscale: 2026-12-10 (one-off 25k), 2026-11-02 (trial increment), 2025-09-14 (helpdesk manual grant). The cadence is mildly concerning but not conclusive of fraud.
- IP analysis shows overlapping CIDR blocks for runs launched within 10 minutes of each other — suggests internal parallel runs rather than distinct external actors.
- No evidence of multiple distinct payment sources or fake billing addresses.
- Customer reputation: known company, public product, existing inbound pipeline.

Recommendation:
- Approve a conditional, timeboxed 25k token grant (half of request) to finish evaluation, not the full 50k — lowers risk exposure.
- Require SSO or confirmation of org admin ownership before enabling the grant.
- Place account on a 30-day monitoring window and escalate any further extension requests to security/compliance.
- Legal to prepare an addendum that converts the credit into a prepaid credit if they decide to convert within 30 days.

Attachments: abuse_analysis_notes.txt (plain text, 6KB)

If sales wants to be more generous given the deal potential, propose they sign a short-term paid pilot commitment to cover the additional tokens.

— Priyom
Security & Risk Analyst | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gutierrez <maria@upscale.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot credit appeal — policy boundary review and conditional extension

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the details and for the quick turnaround. We've reviewed usage and risk signals internally. Given Upscale's clear procurement motion and the lack of strong fraud indicators, Redwood will approve a one-time, conditional extension: 25,000 token-equivalent credit to the existing projects, active immediately and expiring in 7 days.

Conditions:
- Redwood requires org admin confirmation or SSO setup prior to enabling the credit (please provide contact info for your IT admin).
- Legal will issue a short addendum documenting the one-time credit; the addendum will include conversion terms if Upscale converts to a paid contract within 30 days.
- The account will be monitored for unusual patterns for 30 days; any attempt to request further extensions will require escalation to Security Leadership.

Karthik / Ben: please coordinate activation, confirm the token quantity applied to the two project ids, and get CS to schedule an onboarding session with Upscale this week. Priyom: mark the account in the monitoring queue and share the analysis notes with Legal.

Maria — if this sounds acceptable, please reply with your IT admin contact and I will loop in Legal. We want to keep the pilot moving while protecting the platform.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
